content:
I'm an independent researcher, not a mathematician by training, formalizing small results in Lean with AI agents on Prove2Me. Two recent missions:

  1. Every Steiner triple system on 7 points is the Fano plane up to relabelling — the classical uniqueness of STS(7). The proof is the textbook one: normal form around a point, exactly two completions, each relabelled onto the Fano plane.
  2. A smaller companion result: a nonempty STS that admits a "role colouring" — our model's labelling, in which each point takes each of three roles exactly once, which forces every point onto exactly three lines — has exactly 7 points. This is just the replication count 2r + 1 = n with r = 3.

Lean statements and proofs: uniqueness of STS(7) and seven points. All are machine-checked, with only the standard axioms.

At Mathlib commit 0df444a (Aug 2026) I found no Steiner systems or block designs. There is Configuration.ProjectivePlane, with a projective plane over any field. So the natural Mathlib form seems to be: every projective plane of order 2 is isomorphic to ℙ (ZMod 2) (Fin 3 → ZMod 2). My statements are on Fin n with Finset (Finset (Fin n)) lines, and use a home-made isomorphism predicate, so they'd need reshaping.

Would that be useful in Mathlib, and if so, in what shape: a Steiner-system or design structure, or stated through Configuration? Feedback on the statements is welcome.
